- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — reduce forecast by 10–15% in the next 3–5 days.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (prices falling after peaks), model often fails to correct — adjust forecast downward by 5–8% for 2–4 days.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 3–7% immediately.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 1.00, 0.33), model overfits short-term momentum — dampen forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days.
